title: SSE streaming breadcrumbs and quick repro notes
content:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent client hangs or huge RTTs when consuming text-generation SSE from local dev proxy (sometimes only on big models or long outputs).
- Seen both: (a) clients that stop receiving new SSE events for 10–30s then a burst, (b) clients that slowly drain but accumulate memory (chunks kept in app code).
- Appears more frequent when proxying through local devproxy (localhost:8080) vs directly to worker. Could be backpressure/flush behavior at proxy layer.

Quick notes / heuristics I keep hitting:
- curl -N/--no-buffer seems to behave differently than Node fetch (fetch may buffer until newline?).
- Some clients expect final newline after "data: ..." block; missing trailing newline can delay event delivery.
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked + wrong chunk framing on server can produce partial chunk deliveries.
- Nagle/TCP coalescing on loopback sometimes hides problem, but visible when using remote hosts.

Repro matrix (what I tried):
- Env A: local devproxy (localhost:8080) -> worker (localhost:8081) (both started via dev run).
- Env B: bypass proxy, hit worker directly.
- Model sizes: small (redwood-mini), medium (redwood-base), large (redwood-rlhf-1).
- Payload lengths: short prompt (<=128 tokens), verbose prompt (stream ~2k tokens).
- Concurrent clients: 1, 10, 50.

Commands & minimal repros (copy-paste friendly)
1) Basic curl SSE (unix):
   curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-base","input":"Write a 2000 token monologue about seashells"}' \
     http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/generate
   Notes: -N to disable curl buffering. Watching bytes arrive: `pv -bar -s 2000` can show bursts.

2) Python quick stream (requests):
   import requests
   url = "http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/generate"
   headers = {"Accept":"text/event-stream","Authorization":"Bearer test-token"}
   r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"redwood-rlhf-1","input":"long"}, stream=True)
   for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
       print(f"CHUNK ({len(chunk)}): {chunk[:80]!r}")
   Notes: sometimes iter_content yields b'' or stalls; add r.raw.read(1) to confirm blocking behavior.

3) Node fetch + ReadableStream (chromium/node 20):
   const res = await fetch('http://localhost:8080/v1/streams/generate', {
     method: 'POST',
     headers: {'Accept': 'text/event-stream','Authorization':'Bearer test-token','Content-Type':'application/json'},
     body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-base', input: '...'})
   });
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   while (true) {
     const {value, done} = await reader.read();
     if (done) break;
     console.log('BYTES', value && value.length);
   }
   Observed: sometimes read() blocks a long time and then returns a bunch.

4) Minimal Go (http.Client, Transport with DisableCompression true):
   - Use http.Transport{DisableCompression: true, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100} to avoid server-side compression confusing streaming.

Observed server-side logs (snips):
- [2026-02-24 14:12:33.092] stream-session id=abc123 write: 512 bytes
- [2026-02-24 14:12:33.094] stream-session id=abc123 flush: 0ms
- [2026-02-24 14:12:43.197] stream-session id=abc123 write: 4096 bytes
- => 10s gap between writes, client perceives single big chunk.
- Correlated with worker GC spikes (p99 heap growth) on large-model runs.

Error snippets seen on clients:
- Node: "DOMException: The user aborted a request." (seen when app cancels)
- Curl: connection stays open but no bytes for 15s, then bursts.
- Python: r.raw.read() returns b'' then later yields data (weird).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Proxy buffering: local devproxy buffers output until internal buffer threshold or timer, then flushes — causing bursts. Behavior depends on chunk sizes and timer settings.
2) Backend kernel scheduling: large-model kernel work causes long pauses between tokens on worker; runtime aggregates output before returning to http writer.
3) HTTP/1.1 chunking framing bug: writer writes small chunks but with wrong chunk-size framing, client discards until full frame.
4) TLS side-effect: when proxying TLS -> plaintext or vice versa, buffering introduced by TLS library.
5) Application-level: SSE events missing trailing double-newline (\n\n) which some clients need to treat event as finished.

Quick verification checks:
- curl -v output to inspect headers and see if Transfer-Encoding: chunked present.
- tcpdump -A -s0 port 8080 to see raw bytes on wire (confirm whether bytes are sent immediately or batched).
- strace -tt -e write <pid> on proxy to timestamp syscalls.
- run with env DEBUG_STREAM_FLUSH=1 (local flag I added) to print flush calls.

What fixed it temporarily
- For a quick test, adding a forced flush after every token write in the worker (ws/writer.Flush()) made events arrive smoothly. Not production-worthy (too many syscalls) but isolates the issue to flush timing.
- Increasing devproxy FlushInterval from 100ms -> 10ms reduced bursts but increased CPU.

Open action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add tcpdump capture and attach to INFR-7891.
- [ ] Add small benchmark harness that emits known token cadence (1 token/sec) so we can measure client delivery times reproducibly.
- [ ] Try disabling Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) on proxy client/server sockets.
- [ ] Test with http2 vs http1.1 — see if h2 flow control improves/worsens.
- [ ] Re-run with gzip disabled inbound/outbound to rule out compression buffering.
- [ ] Get kernel pprof / jemalloc stats during big-model run to confirm GC pauses.

Notes for next person (short checklist):
- When opening a PR, reference INFR-7891 and attach: tcpdump (pcap), curl -v transcript, and server write timestamps.
- Useful commands I keep in my zshrc:
  alias ssecurl='curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d'
  # raw tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap port 8080

Random breadcrumbs I scribbled while investigating:
- saw extra CR (\r) prepended to data: lines occasionally -> mapping bug in SSE formatter?
- one worker had older vendored http library (1.4.2) that changed flush semantics -> upgrade in staging helped

If you pick this up: start by running curl -v and tcpdump simultaneously. Check server write timestamps (I added a small helper: tools/stream-flush-trace) to triage whether bytes leave the process immediately or are delayed upstream.

End notes: this doc is informal — meant to be a living scratchpad while I iterate. If you update, keep a short changelog at top.

Changelog:
- 2026-03-05: added python/Node repro and hypotheses; noted temporary fix (forced flush)
- 2026-02-24: initial notes and server log excerpts
